name: smolagents WasmExecutor (Pyodide in Deno, executor_type="wasm")
source: https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents (Apache-2.0); WasmExecutor added in v1.20.0 (PR #1261), removed in v1.26.0 (commit fd871374, PR #2321)
pinned: smolagents 1.25.0 from PyPI (last release with WasmExecutor); Deno 2.9.8 on the host; npm:pyodide resolved at runtime to 314.0.8; deno.land/std unpinned, resolved to 0.224.0
engine: Pyodide (CPython compiled to wasm32) inside a Deno process started with --allow-net=<local server>,cdn.jsdelivr.net,pypi and --allow-read/--allow-write scoped to its cache dir
how_run: WasmExecutor(additional_imports=[], logger), send_tools({'lookup': Lookup()}), then executor(code); harness sets DEFAULT_SERVER_PORT to 41980+n and TMPDIR to a canonical scratch path (see surprises).

source_notes.finding: Removed upstream: v1.26.0 deleted WasmExecutor and its docs (commit fd871374, "Remove remote WasmExecutor (#2321)", 2026-05-29). The current release cannot select executor_type="wasm".
Same as other remote executors: tool classes are turned into source with instance_to_source and defined inside Pyodide.
Python POSTs {code, packages} to a Deno HTTP server with a bearer token; no path back to host tools.
Two layers: Pyodide has no processes and an in-memory FS; Deno permissions deny host files, env and subprocesses, and limit network to three hosts. The probes matched this.
Only the 60 s client read timeout. The runner is single-threaded JS, so a stuck snippet blocks every later request until the server is restarted.
The runner imports https://deno.land/std/http/server.ts and npm:pyodide without versions, so each fresh cache resolves whatever is latest (here std 0.224.0 and Pyodide 314.0.8).

surprises: On macOS the default WasmExecutor fails to start: tempfile returns /var/folders/..., Deno canonicalizes reads to /private/var/folders/..., and the --allow-read grant does not match (out/startup-default-tmpdir.txt). Setting TMPDIR to a non-symlinked path fixes it.

Run from a temp dir inside a repo with package.json, Deno adopted that repo as its workspace, used its node_modules Pyodide (0.27.8) and wrote deno.lock at the repo root. The harness now uses a temp dir outside the repo; the stray deno.lock entries were removed.
os.system inside Pyodide kills the whole Deno server (exit 1) rather than raising, so one snippet can take the executor down.
The 60 s timeout frees the caller but not the server: after an infinite loop, every later call times out.
The executor was removed in 1.26.0; the docs that called it a secure option went with it.
